formulas.name: Objective
formulas.where: All procedures below search for a partition of high modularity \(Q\) (defined in the modularity concept); maximizing it is NP-hard (Brandes et al. 2008), so most procedures are heuristics, and the exact search is feasible only on small graphs.

formulas.name: Louvain move gain (Blondel et al. 2008)
formulas.where: Gain of moving the isolated node \(i\) into community \(C\); nodes are moved while the gain is positive, then communities are aggregated into nodes and the step repeated. The visiting order and tie handling are not fixed by the definition, so results depend on them. Leiden (Traag et al. 2019) adds a refinement that keeps communities connected and well separated.

formulas.name: Greedy agglomeration (Clauset, Newman and Moore 2004)
formulas.where: Repeatedly merge the pair of communities with the largest \(\Delta Q\) (adjacent pairs only); the best level of the dendrogram is the maximum of \(Q\) along the merge sequence.

formulas.name: Leading eigenvector (Newman 2006)
formulas.where: A group is split by the signs of the leading eigenvector \(u_1\) of its (generalized) modularity matrix when the leading eigenvalue is positive; repeated until no split raises \(Q\). Zero components (isolated nodes) and repeated eigenvalues leave the split undetermined.

variants.louvain_modularity: Louvain communities of an undirected network by greedy modularity moves and aggregation, scored by modularity (a randomized procedure; the resulting \(Q\) differs between runs).
variants.louvain_quality: The same Louvain procedure judged by the modularity it reaches, averaged over seeds (the comparison is of distributions, not of single runs).
variants.cnx_louvain_seeded: Louvain with a fixed random seed: one reproducible run of the procedure.
variants.leiden: Leiden communities of an undirected network: local moving, refinement into connected groups and aggregation.
variants.cnx_leiden_seeded: Leiden with a fixed random seed.
variants.fast_greedy: The greedy agglomeration of Clauset, Newman and Moore: returns the best level, its modularity and the merge sequence.
variants.cnx_greedy_modularity: Greedy modularity communities by repeated best merges (the Clauset-Newman-Moore procedure).
variants.cnx_naive_greedy: The greedy merging written as a direct search over all pairs of communities (the same objective, compared by the modularity of the whole merged partition).
variants.cnx_naive_greedy_nx: The same naive greedy merging, with whole-partition modularities compared in set order.
variants.leading_eigen: The leading eigenvector method: repeated modularity-matrix splits; returns the membership, its modularity and the number of splits.
variants.optimal_modularity: A partition of maximum modularity found exactly (a Russian doll search or integer programming): the maximum value is determined, the partition need not be unique.
variants.cat_hierarchy_louvain: Documented for scikit-network as the Louvain hierarchy (levels of aggregation); not recorded in detail.
variants.cat_iteration_louvain: Documented for scikit-network as a Louvain iteration; not recorded in detail.

formulas.name: Fluid communities (Pares et al. 2018)
formulas.where: Starting from \(k\) random nodes, each in its own community of density 1, nodes are visited in random order and take the community with the largest summed density among the node itself and its neighbours \(N[v]\); the sweeps repeat until no node changes. formulas.name: Girvan-Newman procedure (Girvan and Newman 2002)
formulas.where: Edges between communities carry many shortest paths and are removed first; the removal sequence defines a dendrogram. Edges of equal betweenness are removed in an order the definition does not fix.

is_partition.note: Documented only (NetworkX), never run; the condition is stated from its definition, with no primary paper.

notation.meaning: graph with node set \(V\), \(n=|V|\); every edge has a source and a target (the ends of an undirected edge are interchangeable)
a collection of node sets

formulas.name: Partition test
formulas.latex: \{S_i\}\text{ is a partition of }V\iff\bigcup_iS_i=V\ \text{and}\ S_i\cap S_j=\emptyset\ (i\ne j)\ \text{and}\ S_i\ne\emptyset
formulas.where: The sets cover all nodes, no node is in two sets (a cover that allows overlap is not a partition); empty sets are normally excluded.

variants.cat_is_partition@community: True when the collection of node sets is a partition of the node set.

edge_cases.definition_gives: The empty collection partitions the empty node set.
Overlapping sets or missing nodes make it false.
